summary: Fixed examples/flashlight/run.py so the flashlight and capture controller polling no longer constructs FKey via game.get_unreal_object(uclass='FKey'). The code now passes an FKey-shaped struct argument ({"KeyName": key_name}) directly to APlayerController.IsInputKeyDown, allowing SPEAR's function-call struct deserialization path to handle FKey.
work_completed: Updated is_input_key_down() and was_input_key_pressed_since_last_poll() to pass FKey struct data directly without the unused game argument.
Kept default flashlight toggle target as Gamepad_FaceButton_Right, matching Xbox B / face button right.
Kept terminal Enter pose capture intact; controller capture still uses args.capture_key when --capture-poses is enabled.
Ran syntax verification: python -m py_compile examples/flashlight/run.py.

findings.message: Root cause: FKey is a Unreal struct used as a function parameter, not a UObject class. Calling game.get_unreal_object(uclass='FKey') asks SPEAR for a UObject/default object class path and triggers the runtime Exception: 'FKey' seen after logging Flashlight toggle key: Gamepad_FaceButton_Right.
Fix: IsInputKeyDown now receives Key={"KeyName": key_name}, which matches the FKey struct field shape and avoids direct FKey object construction.

Manual verification command: python examples/flashlight/run.py --capture-poses. Test Xbox B / Unreal key Gamepad_FaceButton_Right to toggle the flashlight; press Enter in the terminal to capture a pose.
